title: Evidence Manifest
description: Evidence artefacts and their receipts. A receipt binds an artefact to the configuration it was collected against, who collected it and when. Without one, 'this test passed' is a claim about an unnamed artefact from an unnamed party at an unknown time against an unknown configuration — an assertion, not evidence.

state.description: Lifecycle of the ARTEFACT. Applicability to a particular claim lives on the graph edge, not here: one artefact can stop justifying one claim while still justifying another at the same instant, which a single node-level state cannot express.

source_kind.description: Where it came from: inspect_eval, config_snapshot, control_test, attestation, runtime_log, contract_attestation.

scope_passport_digest.description: Passport the artefact was collected against. Divergence from the case's current Passport is reported but does NOT on its own invalidate: after any change every artefact predates the new Passport, so treating staleness as invalidation would collapse the whole case. Severed edges decide.

quality.description: Five dimensions, recorded separately and NEVER averaged. Strong provenance concealing weak ecological validity is exactly the failure an average produces: one says the artefact is traceable, the other says it resembles production, and they are not interchangeable.

provenance.description: Can this be traced to the run and code that produced it?

coverage.description: How much of the relevant space was exercised?

construct_validity.description: Does the test actually measure the claim? A human judgement; no log can evidence it.

ecological_validity.description: Did the environment resemble production? Also a human judgement.

repeatability.description: Would a re-run produce the same result?
